title: A spatial view of tumor neoantigen recognition - Nature Biotechnology
gist: A short Nature Biotechnology research briefing (abstract-only landing page, body behind subscription) summarising Nagler et al.: a single-cell spatial transcriptomics framework that maps neoantigen-expressing tumor cells alongside tumor-infiltrating T cells and adds T cell receptor sequencing, revealing distinct immune niches in the tumor microenvironment that determine tumor-specific responses.

insights.claim: A single-cell spatial transcriptomics framework can now map neoantigen-expressing tumor cells and tumor-infiltrating T cells together with T cell receptor sequencing, closing a gap in which cell-by-cell interactions between the two populations were largely unexplored.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Adds a new measurable readout — physical proximity of a T cell to its cognate tumor cell — that neoantigen vaccine and TCR-therapy developers can use as a biomarker.
insights.quote: The cell-by-cell interactions between neoantigen-expressing tumor cells and tumor-specific T cells remained largely unexplored.

insights.claim: The approach reveals distinct immune niches inside the tumor microenvironment whose properties determine whether tumor-specific responses occur, implying spatial organisation is causal for antitumor immunity rather than incidental.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If niche structure gates response, spatial assays become a patient-selection tool for immunotherapy — a diagnostics market adjacent to the therapy itself.
insights.quote: This approach reveals distinct immune niches in the tumor microenvironment and their properties that determine tumor-specific responses.

insights.claim: Many T cells found in human tumor infiltrates are bystander CD8+ T cells that are phenotypically distinct, which is why identifying genuinely antigen-specific antitumor responses has been a persistent challenge.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Bystander contamination is the reason simple TIL counts fail as biomarkers — any assay that separates cognate from bystander T cells has real clinical pricing power.
insights.locator: Simoni, Y. et al. reference annotation

insights.claim: The briefing anchors the work in an existing personalized-cancer-immunotherapy stack — neoantigen frameworks, large HLA class I peptidome datasets for epitope prediction, Slide-tags single-nucleus spatial genomics, and adoptive cell transfer — positioning spatial genotyping as the missing measurement layer rather than a new therapy.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Tools sit upstream of therapy value capture — the near-term commercial beneficiaries are spatial-genomics platform vendors, not drug developers.
